description: Modern Jira REST API client for JavaScript and TypeScript — the Jira Cloud platform, Agile, and Service Management APIs, with every response validated at runtime.
rules: Install with `npm install jira.js`, which gives you version 6. The package is ESM-only and requires Node.js 22+; there is no CommonJS build, so `require('jira.js')` does not work.

Build a client with a factory: `createCloudClient` for the Jira Cloud platform API, `createAgileClient` for boards/sprints/backlog, `createServiceDeskClient` for Jira Service Management, `createTeamsClient` for the organization-level Teams API, `createAssetsClient` for Assets — which takes a `workspaceId` and its own configuration, because it answers on `api.atlassian.com` rather than on your site. The `Version2Client`/`Version3Client` classes were removed in 6.0 and have no direct replacement — there is one platform surface now.

Need more than one surface? Build the client once with `createClient` from `jira.js/core` and pass that same client to each factory. Two clients mean two OAuth token states, and because Atlassian rotates the refresh token, whichever refreshes first invalidates the other.

Provide `host` as the bare site URL (e.g. `https://your-domain.atlassian.net`) — the API path belongs to the request, not to `host`. It is required for basic and bearer auth. With OAuth 2.0 it is optional and ignored: the cloudId is resolved automatically and requests route through `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/{cloudId}`.

Authentication is the `auth` field, a discriminated union on `type`: `{ type: 'basic', email, apiToken }`, `{ type: 'bearer', token }`, or `{ type: 'oauth2', clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken, onTokenRefresh }`. Use an Atlassian API token, never an account password.

Atlassian rotates the OAuth 2.0 refresh token on every refresh and invalidates the previous one — persist the new value from the `onTokenRefresh` callback, or the next process start will fail to authenticate.
Never expose `clientSecret` in a browser; OAuth 2.0 token refresh is server-side only.
JWT (Atlassian Connect) is NOT supported in 6.0 and has no replacement. Integrations that authenticate Connect installations with a shared secret must stay on `jira.js@5`.
Every endpoint method takes a single typed parameters object and returns a Promise. Callbacks were removed in 6.0 — there is no Node-style callback argument.

Failed requests reject with typed errors: `ApiError` and its subclasses `AuthError`, `ScopeError`, `ForbiddenError`, `NotFoundError`, `RateLimitError` (with `retryAfterMs`), `ServerError`, plus `NetworkError`, `OAuthError`, `ConfigError` and `SchemaMismatchError`. Detect them with the predicates (`isNotFoundError`, `isRateLimitError`, …) rather than `instanceof`, which breaks under bundling, minification and duplicate installs.

Responses are validated against Zod schemas. A mismatch does NOT throw by default: the body is returned unvalidated and the problem is reported once per field on stderr. Configure with `onSchemaMismatch: 'warn' | 'silent' | 'throw' | (report) => void`. Use `'throw'` in test suites.

Rich text fields (comment bodies, issue descriptions) accept either an Atlassian Document Format document or a wiki-markup string; a string is routed through Jira's v2 endpoint and read back, so it still formats. Reads always return a document, never a string.
Retries are off by default. Opt in with `retry: { maxAttempts, initialDelayMs, backoffFactor }` — it covers network errors and 502/503/504 only, never 4xx (including 429) or other 5xx.
`getAttachmentContent` accepts an optional `range` (HTTP Range header, e.g. `bytes=0-1023`) for partial/byte-range downloads, returning 206 Partial Content.

For smaller bundles import the flat per-endpoint functions from `jira.js/cloud`, `jira.js/agile` or `jira.js/serviceDesk` and pass the client as the first argument, e.g. `getIssue(client, { issueIdOrKey })`. Those subpaths also carry every parameter and response type. They are not re-exported from the package root because the surfaces collide on some names.

Webhooks go the other way — Jira posts to a server of yours — so `jira.js/webhooks` is types only and compiles to nothing: `WebhookPayload` is a union of fifty-seven events discriminated by `webhookEvent`, and `WebhookHeaders` types the headers in lower case, as Node delivers them, with every value a string including the retry count. Cast the parsed body and headers; there is no parser and no signature verification, because a webhook body is shaped by the site that sent it. Atlassian documents only the issue payload, so that is the one group whose entity is required — everywhere else the entity field is optional.
